title: One distributor, four tracing rules, four answers
summary: ₹4.5 lakh of fraud money mixes into a pharma distributor's busy account; FIFO, LIFO, pro-rata and LIBR disagree, and LienLine shows the range and why LIBR is used.

complaint.narrative: A WhatsApp 'stock tips' group promised 4% a week. On 24 Sep at 10:05 I sent Rs 6,00,000 by NEFT to XXXX4935 at Konark Small Finance Bank (UTR 626707951584). The app stopped working the same evening.

From: SI P. Malviya, Cyber PS, Indore

grievances.text: We sold medicines against a genuine invoice. Our working capital of ₹7.5 lakh is frozen.
We were paid by our distributor for supplies. Our account is frozen in full.

reasons.text: The victim's money arrived via T1 (₹6,00,000.00 of ₹6,00,000.00 from A1). The balance fell to ₹5,800.00 after T4, which caps what can still be traced: ₹5,800.00 under LIBR (lowest intermediate balance).
Mule signals present (Account opened 50 days ago; 99% of available funds passed straight through), but no registry hit and fewer than 3 linked complaints, so a full freeze is not justified.

Other tracing rules give FIFO ₹5,800.00, LIFO ₹5,000.00, PRO_RATA ₹5,792.28. LIBR is used because it is the accepted standard for mixed funds: it never counts the holder's later, clean credits as the victim's money.

The victim's money arrived via T2 (₹4,49,200.00 of ₹4,50,000.00 from A2). The balance fell to ₹3,50,000.00 after T8, which caps what can still be traced: ₹3,50,000.00 under LIBR (lowest intermediate balance).

The current hold of ₹7,50,000.00 covers the whole balance. MP High Court, Archana v State of MP, 27 Jul 2026 and Rajasthan High Court, Shree Balaji Enterprises v RBI, 20 Aug 2026 limit a hold to the identifiable disputed amount, so ₹4,00,000.00 is released.

Nothing is traceable here under LIBR: T6 (₹0.00 of ₹6,00,000.00 from A3) carried ₹0.00 of the victim's money because the payer's own funds covered each payment.

letters.to: Branch Manager, Konark Small Finance Bank
letters.subject: Instruction to Replace Whole-Account Freeze with Lien on Account XXXX4935
letters.body:
This letter serves as a formal instruction regarding the hold placed on Account XXXX4935, held by Manoj Pal.

This action follows the NCRP acknowledgement 31509260077777 and the notice under Section 106 BNSS dated 26 Sep 2026 from SI P. Malviya, Cyber PS, Indore. The current hold is on the whole balance of ₹5,800.00.

Based on the decision derived from MP High Court, Archana v State of MP, 27 Jul 2026, and Rajasthan High Court, Shree Balaji Enterprises v RBI, 20 Aug 2026, the hold must be limited to the identifiable disputed amount. The credit received via UTR 626707951584, amounting to ₹6,00,000.00, has ₹6,00,000.00 traceable to the complaint under LIBR.

Therefore, you are instructed to replace the whole-account freeze with a lien of ₹5,800.00, which is the amount traceable under the lowest intermediate balance rule. Kindly release ₹0.00 from the existing hold.

Nodal Officer, Konark Small Finance Bank

letters.subject: Instruction to Replace Whole-Account Freeze with Lien on Account XXXX4193
letters.body:
This letter serves as a formal instruction regarding the hold placed on account XXXX4193, held by Malwa Pharma Distributors.

Reference is made to the NCRP acknowledgement 31509260077777 and the notice under Section 106 BNSS dated 26 Sep 2026 from SI P. Malviya, Cyber PS, Indore. The current hold is on the whole balance of ₹7,50,000.00.

Based on the decision derived from MP High Court, Archana v State of MP, 27 Jul 2026, and Rajasthan High Court, Shree Balaji Enterprises v RBI, 20 Aug 2026, the hold must be limited to the identifiable disputed amount. The traceable amount under the lowest intermediate balance rule is ₹3,50,000.00.

Therefore, you are instructed to replace the whole-account freeze with a lien of ₹3,50,000.00 on account XXXX4193. The remaining amount of ₹4,00,000.00 must be released from the hold. This instruction pertains to the credit received via UTR 626769080818, where ₹4,49,200.00 is traceable to the complaint under LIBR.

Nodal Officer, Sahyadri Bank

letters.subject: Reply to Grievance Regarding Hold on Account XXXX4193
letters.body:
This is in reference to the grievance received on 29 Sep 2026 concerning the hold placed on your account, XXXX4193, held with Sahyadri Bank.

We acknowledge the NCRP acknowledgement 31509260077777 and the notice under Section 106 BNSS dated 26 Sep 2026 from SI P. Malviya, Cyber PS, Indore. The current hold amount is ₹7,50,000.00.

Based on the legal precedents set by MP High Court, Archana v State of MP, 27 Jul 2026, and Rajasthan High Court, Shree Balaji Enterprises v RBI, 20 Aug 2026, a hold is limited to the identifiable disputed amount. We have reviewed the credit via UTR 626769080818 for ₹4,50,000.00, of which ₹4,49,200.00 is traceable to the complaint under LIBR.

Consequently, we have decided to impose a lien of ₹3,50,000.00, representing the amount traceable under the lowest intermediate balance rule, and release ₹4,00,000.00 from the hold. Further updates will be provided as necessary.

letters.subject: Instruction to Release Hold on Account XXXX2505
letters.body:
This letter serves as a formal instruction regarding the hold placed on Account XXXX2505, held by Indore Medical Agencies, Narmada Bank.

This hold was initiated following a cyber-fraud complaint, referenced by NCRP acknowledgement 31509260077777 and the notice under Section 106 BNSS dated 26 Sep 2026 from SI P. Malviya, Cyber PS, Indore. The current hold amount is ₹9,00,000.00.

Upon review, it has been determined that no amount is traceable to the complaint under LIBR. Specifically, the credit received via UTR 626527649190 for ₹6,00,000.00 has ₹0.00 traceable to the complaint.

In light of the legal precedents set by MP High Court, Archana v State of MP, 27 Jul 2026, and Rajasthan High Court, Shree Balaji Enterprises v RBI, 20 Aug 2026, which limit holds to identifiable disputed amounts, you are hereby instructed to release the entire hold of ₹9,00,000.00 in full. The traceable amount is ₹0.00.

Nodal Officer, Narmada Bank

Nodal Officer, Narmada Bank
